🤔 Fly around the world and you land fractionally younger than everyone who stayed. This has been measured.
Name it before the reveal — comment your guess 👇

ANSWER: Time Dilation

In 1971 Hafele and Keating flew atomic clocks on commercial airliners and found exactly the predicted offset, tens of nanoseconds. It's not an illusion or a clock fault — moving clocks genuinely tick slower. ✈️

uncertainty-principle.caption:
🤔 This isn't about clumsy instruments. It's a statement about what a particle actually has.
Got it? Say it out loud, then keep watching 👀

ANSWER: The Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle

Position and momentum aren't simultaneously well-defined, because a particle is a wave and a wave can't be both localised and single-frequency. Perfect instruments wouldn't help. It's also why atoms don't collapse. ⚛️

wiens-law.caption:
🤔 Everything glows, including you. The colour of the glow tells you the temperature, and nothing else.
Comment your answer before it appears on screen 💬

ANSWER: Wien's Displacement Law

Peak wavelength is inversely proportional to temperature, so hot stars look blue and cool ones red. You peak in the infrared at about 10 microns, which is precisely what a thermal camera is built to see. 🔥
